Q: Custom swimming entity (Animal) won't move in water A:

If you're using Mojang mappings, WaterAnimalEntity doesn’t exist under that name. The Mojang-mapped equivalent is AgeableWaterCreature.

So instead of extending Animal, use:

public class WhaleEntity extends AgeableWaterCreature

AgeableWaterCreature already includes the correct aquatic behavior used by mobs like dolphins, which prevents issues like floating to the surface or being launched out of the water.

Q: Connecting to SQL Server from R studios: "Error: nanodbc/nanodbc.cpp:983: 00000: [unixODBC][Driver Manager]Can't open lib 'driver' : file not found" A:

I go for Driver = "SQL Server", it works for me.

Q: Error: Installation of TensorFlow not found A:

This is what I did:

I first installed the Anaconda ensuring that it is in my root path.

I proceeded to install the tensorflow and the reticulate packages from github using the devtools package.

# Install devtools
install.packages(“devtools”)

# Install tensorflow:
devtools::install_github(“rstudio/tensorflow”)

# install reticulate:
install.packages("reticulate")

The reticulate package provides a comprehensive set of tools for ease of interaction between Python and R.

Now load the reticulate package:

# Load library
library(reticulate)

Select the python version you would like to use in your environment. This should sort the problem where you have multiple python versions installed in your system:

# Python version
use_python("/usr/local/bin/python")

Now, set the virtual environment in which we will perform your analysis:

# Python environment:
use_virtualenv("myenv")

Now proceed to install tensorflow:

library(tensorflow)

# Install tensorflow
install_tensorflow()

To test if tensforflow has been installed:

tf$print(
  tf$constant('Hello, TensorFlow!')
  )

Q: artifactory as docker registry A:

| | Subdomain (recommended) | docker login myrepo.artifactory.example.com | docker push myrepo.artifactory.example.com/image:tag | | Repository path | docker login artifactory.example.com | docker push artifactory.example.com/myrepo/image:tag | | Port | docker login artifactory.example.com:8082 | docker push artifactory.example.com:8082/myrepo/image:tag |

Key points for 7.x:

  • The Docker API runs on port 8082 (not 8081)
  • A reverse proxy is required for subdomain and repository path methods
  • For self-signed certs, add to Docker's daemon.json: "insecure-registries": ["your-server:8082"]
  • You can only push to local repositories (not remote/virtual)

400 Bad Request on login? You're likely using the wrong access method for your repo config. Check which method your repo is configured for in the Artifactory UI.
